   金利がじりじりと上昇し続ける中、株価はほとんど下落した。 S&P500は0.1%下落、ナスダックは0.3%下落した。 １０年米国債利回りは０．０４％ポイント上昇し４．６９７％となった。

Oil Surges With No Hormuz Deal in Sight
 
Plus, Nvidia’s big deal and Intel’s share sale
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
STRINGER/REUTERS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Oil prices jumped after negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz turned south once again. Over the weekend, a top Iranian official laid out a series of tough demands for opening the Strait, and the United Arab Emirates said Iran launched a missile attack on one of its ships. Front-month Brent crude gained $4.17 per barrel, or 4.99% to $87.72.

 

Stocks were mostly lower as rates kept creeping higher. The S&P 500 fell 0.1% and the Nasdaq declined 0.3%. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 0.04 percentage point to 4.697%.

 

Nvidia reached a mammoth financing deal with leading Wall Street firms. Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR agreed to help Nvidia raise $500 billion to fund the AI infrastructure build-out, the Wall Street Journal reported. Apollo and Blackstone rose 3.6% and 3.3% respectively while Nvidia fell 2.9%.

 

Intel said it would sell $15 billion of new shares. Capitalizing on the stock’s strong performance since granting a stake to the Federal government, Intel moved to raise fresh funds. The chipmaker cited strong customer demand “driven by unprecedented investment in AI compute.” Its shares fell 4.1%.

One Big Story

 

Private credit is showing increasing signs of stress, despite comments to the contrary from some of the largest fund managers that are trying to put a year of turmoil behind them.

 

Recent quarterly reports from funds overseen by the industry’s big players showed that loan health and investor returns are worsening, according to an analysis by The Wall Street Journal.
